solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Noble European artist very taken by Mrs Simpson (8)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the artist and 'very' are taken in by Marge, held inside her name

blocks.note: Marge Simpson, Homer's wife in The Simpsons
RA = Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
v = very, as in musical and dictionary shorthand

annotation.surface: A European aristocrat taking up with Marge Simpson, of all people.
annotation.walkthrough: The artist and 'very' go inside Marge together. A margrave was a German noble, originally the lord of a border province.
annotation.definitionFit: A margrave is a hereditary noble title in the old German states.

entries.clue: Cut almost plausibly fluent figure in the jungle (6)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: its last letter is left off

blocks.note: to mow is to cut grass
GLIB (plausibly fluent) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Praise for someone who talks their way through the jungle a little too smoothly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plausibly fluent' is a two-word definition of GLIB, which is easy to read as describing the figure instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Mowgli is the boy raised by wolves in Kipling's The Jungle Book.

entries.clue: Simpson put in an appearance, knocked over wine (5)

indicatorNotes.put in: OJ is put inside the other piece
indicatorNotes.knocked over: in a down clue, knocked over turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: an air = an appearance or manner; knocked over it becomes RIA
O. J. Simpson, the American footballer

annotation.surface: A Simpson turns up at a party and knocks the wine over.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the appearance is turned round; the Simpson goes in afterwards. After Marge in 1 across, this Simpson is a different one.
annotation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of Spain.

entries.clue: Full game of golf enjoyed — exhausted! (7)

indicatorNotes.exhausted: emptied: the word loses all its inside letters

blocks.note: a round of golf is one full game
ENJOYED emptied of its middle leaves E…D

annotation.surface: A golfer reports on a full round they enjoyed, and how tired it left them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' looks like the golfer's state at the end of the round; it is the instruction to empty ENJOYED.
annotation.definitionFit: Rounded means full in shape, plump, as in a rounded figure.

entries.clue: Ruined investor quit holding large position in entertainment sector (13)

indicatorNotes.Ruined: the letters of INVESTOR QUIT are wrecked and rebuilt
indicatorNotes.holding: the anagram holds L inside it

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
L = large, as on clothing sizes
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A ruined investor walks away from the entertainment business but keeps a big stake in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all finance — investor, holding, position, sector — and the answer is a stage act.
annotation.definitionFit: Ventriloquist is a job in show business, a position one might hold in entertainment.

entries.clue: Reversing wagon over Joe; how distressing (6)

indicatorNotes.Reversing: the wagon's word is turned to read backwards
indicatorNotes.over: the wagon goes over Joe, covering him on both sides

blocks.note: a cart is a wagon; reversed it is TRAC
GI Joe, the American soldier

annotation.surface: A wagon backs over someone called Joe: an awful accident.
annotation.walkthrough: Joe is not a person's name here but GI Joe, slang for an American soldier.
annotation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something deeply distressing.

entries.clue: Mature East German blocks fencing thrust (7)

indicatorNotes.blocks: OST blocks the word by sitting in the middle of it

blocks.note: ripe = mature
Ost is German for east

annotation.surface: A seasoned East German fencer parries every attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'East German' reads as a nationality, and it means the German word for east.
annotation.definitionFit: A riposte is a fencer's quick return thrust after parrying.

entries.clue: According to Spooner, little Mildred acquired a diver (9)

indicatorNotes.According to Spooner: Dr Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

blocks.note: Millie is a pet form of Mildred; given GOT's G sound it becomes GILLY, spelt GUILLE
got = acquired; given Millie's M sound it becomes MOT

annotation.surface: News that young Millie has got hold of a diver, of whatever kind.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of MILLIE GOT and you say the bird's name.
annotation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird that dives deep under water for fish.

entries.clue: Iron ore, essentially, loaded on board transport vessel (3-5)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its middle letter
indicatorNotes.loaded on board: the iron and ore letters are loaded inside the carrying word

blocks.note: to transport is to carry
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the middle letter of oRe

annotation.surface: Iron ore being loaded aboard a ship for transport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Transport vessel' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'vessel', and 'transport' is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A car ferry is a vessel carrying vehicles across water.

entries.clue: Nowt wrong with Hindu crime fiction (9)

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: anagram fodder; nowt is northern English for nothing
anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A Yorkshire verdict that there is nothing wrong with Hindu crime novels.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a book review, and the whole of 'Nowt wrong with Hindu' is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story in which the reader guesses the culprit.

entries.clue: Planners try at working honestly and openly (13)

indicatorNotes.working: the letters are set working, rearranged into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Planning officials attempt, for once, to work in the open.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is local government trying to be transparent, which is exactly the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Transparently means openly, with nothing hidden.

entries.clue: Previous month, uncovered gold (5)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: the month's covering letters, first and last, are stripped off

blocks.note: APRIL without its first and last letters
or is gold in heraldry

annotation.surface: Last month someone dug up gold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' suggests gold being unearthed; it strips the outer letters from the month. APRIL is the month that works.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prior engagement is one arranged previously.

entries.clue: Skinny daughter sacrificing anything to be a dedicated swimmer (7)

indicatorNotes.sacrificing: the word gives up the letters for 'anything'

blocks.note: lean = skinny
DAUGHTER loses AUGHT (anything), leaving DER

annotation.surface: A thin girl gives up everything to devote herself to swimming.
annotation.walkthrough: Aught is an old word for anything. In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont every night to visit Hero, and drowned doing so.
annotation.definitionFit: Leander's nightly swims for love of Hero make him a truly dedicated swimmer.

entries.clue: Free love recollected by sailors (7)

indicatorNotes.recollected: re-collected: the letters gathered up again in a new order

blocks.note: AB = able seaman, so ABS are sailors
LOVE rearranged

annotation.surface: Sailors fondly remembering free love.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free love' reads as one phrase; 'Free' is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or guilt.

entries.clue: Goes off side in a pleasure boat (6,7)

indicatorNotes.in: the first two pieces go inside the word for 'a'

blocks.note: an egg that addles goes off, turns rotten
a side is a sports team
per = a, as in £5 per head

annotation.surface: A passenger on a pleasure cruise gets off at the side.
annotation.walkthrough: The small word 'a' carries a whole piece, as in 'miles per hour', and the other two sit inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a steamboat driven by paddle wheels, now mostly used for pleasure trips.

entries.clue: Aid camper getting injured? I might (9)

annotation.definition: Aid camper getting injured? I might

indicatorNotes.getting injured: the letters are hurt, knocked out of shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone offering to help a camper who has hurt themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the anagram, and read as a sentence it is the answer speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: A paramedic is exactly the person who might aid an injured camper.

entries.clue: Conservative group overturning No 1 cut affecting mothers (1-7)

indicatorNotes.overturning: in a down clue, the number is turned upside down, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: C = Conservative, the British party
a sect is a group
NO and I (1 as a Roman numeral); overturned it is ION

annotation.surface: A Conservative faction reverses its leader's spending cut to maternity services.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No 1' looks like the leader of the group; it is just NO plus the Roman numeral I.
annotation.definitionFit: A C-section, or caesarean section, is a surgical cut to deliver a baby.

entries.clue: Musical group tight, having consumed two pints, missing second note (6,7)

indicatorNotes.having consumed: the word for tight swallows the two pints
indicatorNotes.missing: a word missing something has lost it, so the tight word goes without its second N

blocks.note: stringent = tight, strict; without its second N it is STRINGET
N = note; this is the second N in the word, removed
a quart is two pints

annotation.surface: A band, drunk after two pints, forgets the second note.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight' pulls towards drunkenness, which the two pints encourage; here it means strict. The tight word has two Ns, and it is the second that goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by type: two violins, viola and cello make the standard chamber ensemble.

entries.clue: Falls once more going over the border of Rwanda (7)

indicatorNotes.going over: in a down clue, going over flips the word, so it reads upwards
indicatorNotes.border of: the border of a word is its outside letters

blocks.note: again = once more; flipped it is NIAGA
the outside letters of RwandA

annotation.surface: Waterfalls once again spilling across the Rwandan frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Falls' opens the clue looking like a verb; it is the definition, a proper noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls lies on the US–Canada border.

entries.clue: Hardy character clutches gospel regularly, having removed hair shirt? (7)

indicatorNotes.clutches: the character holds the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.regularly: every other letter of the word

blocks.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's heroine
the second, fourth and sixth letters of gOsPeL

annotation.surface: A pious Hardy heroine holds her gospel close while doing penance.
annotation.walkthrough: A hair shirt is a penitent's rough garment, and anyone who takes it off is, for the moment, topless; the question mark flags the leap.
annotation.definitionFit: Topless means without a top; removing a hair shirt would leave one so.

entries.clue: Hat that is carrying the head? (6)

blocks.note: bean is slang for head
i.e. = that is

annotation.surface: A riddle: what is it that sits on your head?
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'that is' carries the head on top of it. The question mark flags the pun: a beanie really does carry your head.
annotation.definitionFit: A beanie is a close-fitting knitted hat.

entries.clue: Bitter drink affected game plumber’s guts (7)

indicatorNotes.guts: a word's guts are its inside letters

blocks.note: camp = affected, exaggerated in manner
the inside of mARIo, the plumber of Nintendo's Super Mario games

annotation.surface: A plumber's insides upset by a bitter drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The plumber must be found before his guts can be taken: Mario, the video-game hero. 'Affected' looks like a verb about the drink; it is CAMP.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this bright red Italian aperitif is famous for its bitterness.

entries.clue: Former copper beginning to erupt, go ballistic! (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: ex = former, as in ex-wife
Mr Plod, the policeman in Noddy stories, so British slang for the police
the first letter of Erupt

annotation.surface: A retired policeman about to lose his temper completely.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper is a policeman here, not the metal Cu.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a missile gone ballistic flies out of control, and a person doing so erupts in rage, bursting in the figurative sense.

entries.clue: Over a thousand tapir — wingless animals (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The clue says 'animals', plural, against a word that looks singular; fair because okapi, like sheep, is its own plural.

indicatorNotes.wingless: the word loses its wings, the letters at either end

blocks.note: O = over, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
K = a thousand
TAPIR without its outer letters

annotation.surface: More than a thousand tapirs, and not one of them can fly.
annotation.walkthrough: A tapir is an animal too, which makes the surface look like a definition by itself; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of central Africa related to the giraffe; the plural is also okapi.

entries.clue: Huge country home — help is coming round (5)

indicatorNotes.coming round: the word turns round and reads backwards

blocks.note: in = at home
aid = help; coming round it is DIA

annotation.surface: A grand country house, where help is on its way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge country home' reads as a stately home; the definition stops at 'country'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the seventh-largest nation by area and the most populous on earth.

entries.clue: Place to buy drinks in can that helps to fund the church (5,4)

annotation.definition: that helps to fund the church
annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'something that helps to fund the church'

indicatorNotes.in: the drinking place goes inside the can

blocks.note: the bar is where drinks are bought
a tin is a can

annotation.surface: A collecting tin in the pub, raising money for the church.
annotation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of a parish's produce paid to the church; the tithe barn stored it.
annotation.definitionFit: A tithe barn held the produce given as tithes, the church's funding.

entries.clue: Delicious beverage reportedly downed with pirate’s approval? (6)

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to down it quickly (British slang)
arr, the stage pirate's grunt of assent
said together they make the answer

annotation.surface: A tasty drink knocked back to a pirate's cheer.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits before 'reportedly', so it is the wordplay that is spoken, not the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Nectar, drink of the gods, is any delicious drink.

entries.clue: Always empty rooms to let here in Scotland (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'here' stands for a place, the noun

indicatorNotes.empty: the word is emptied of its middle letters

blocks.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always
RoomS emptied of its middle
to hire out is to let

annotation.surface: Rooms in this place are always standing empty, waiting to be let.
annotation.walkthrough: Ayrshire is a county in south-west Scotland. 'Here' points back to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Ayrshire is a region of Scotland, the place meant by 'here'.
